name: easyeda-pro-control
description: Safety-gated EasyEDA adapters, narrow symbol/PCB workflows and seven engineering skills.

interface.longDescription: Seven skills cover EasyEDA Pro control, schematic design, PCB layout, component libraries, manufacturing release, design review and extension development. Version-pinned typed API adapters distinguish public subsets, native equivalents, vendor HTTP equivalents, blocked implementations and documented omissions. Discovery is not execution support. The exact legacy read tuple is connected-read-admitted and future mismatches fail closed; legacy general writers remain runtime-disabled. Three declaration snapshots cover 835 distinct methods. EasyEDA 3.2.209 offers tools for API reference, local discovery, status, bounded calculations/system/language/viewport and editor/shortcut observations, public catalog search/metadata, ordinary launch and a disposable project/PCB opening lifecycle with layer metadata, copper count and ten primitive-family projections. Catalog queries require explicit network confirmation, support footprint/symbol/device search and known metadata lookup, and run without EasyEDA or SDK execution. Eight optional once-only observation stages retain the original receiver and compare two ordered samples. Primitive projections cover Line, Arc, Via, parentless String, Component, Pad, grouped Attribute, Dimension and Image. The selection/relations stage also captures ordered selected IDs and requested component child-pad lists, correlated with global Pad rows. Separate Pad and Image stages add native top/inner/bottom style groups, transformed M/L/A vector paths and opaque Picture references. Style groups are not physical-layer expansion, and image references do not verify asset bytes or availability. Arc observations retain centers, radii, endpoint radians and direction. Poured observations preserve existing serialized copper contours and parent associations in native ten-mil units without rebuilding or qualifying copper. Reader selection remains subject to the unchanged session command budget. Repeatable digest-bound queries filter published snapshots by exact IDs and supported fields, or return their captured selection and component-pad groups. Historical queries make no live call, adopt no owner and establish no current state. Observations do not prove complete model membership, reciprocal ownership, physical stackup, connectivity or saved contents. Opening can migrate, replay caches and automatically Save; original normal cleanup remains required. A separate disposable project-worker startup route captures original constructor callbacks, current wrapper and publisher relations, and bracketed actor/local-Date observations through retained normal cleanup. It requires explicit debugger-pause acceptance and does not prove complete startup, native channel peers, contained destinations or server-clock provenance. A separate launch-sealed empty-baseline purpose retains the original managed SQL checkpoint, records intent before PCB navigation and joins fixed common data between empty raw-manager samples. It has fixed request, reply-class, aggregate-byte, polling and launch-time budgets, and cannot upgrade an existing startup owner. This sequential observation does not establish full model membership, startup completion or saved-state equality; connected validation remains pending. No general geometry writer, explicit Save, PCB-worker completion or recovery route is registered on209. Source/offline checks and installed snapshots are separate from connected validation. Older profiles retain their exact eligible metadata workflows and disposable validation routes; those proofs do not transfer to209. General writers and ratline capture integration remain unfinished. No unrestricted JavaScript, arbitrary command, Save/Discard choice, force exit or blind retry is exposed. Historical journals cannot recreate ownership. Consult the skills and coverage inventory for exact scope.
